title: SKU bundle + trial & billing preflight
content:
Purpose:
This working doc enumerates the cross-functional preflight checks for launching a bundled SKU that includes a free trial credit, partner co-sell metadata, and meterable billing configuration across cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). The goal is to reduce rework from legal/billing/security reviews during listing submission and to provide a minimal acceptance bar for product, finance, and partner ops to sign off.

Audience:
- Primary: GTM listing owners, Partner Ops, Revenue Ops
- Secondary: Finance (billing), Legal, Product Ops, Engineering (integrations)
content_steps: Executive summary: launch a bundled offering (Core API + Dedicated reserved credits) with a 14-day free trial credit voucher; target channel: AWS and Azure to start; listing type: SaaS (metered) + BYOL/Reserved plan tile where applicable.

Acceptance checklist (must be ✅ before submission):
  - SKU taxonomy mapped and approved by Revenue Ops (product slug, plan code, price id).
  - Trial credit flow instrumented: voucher code generation endpoint + backend redemption toggle.
  - Billing test plan executed in sandbox (billing events validated: activation, usage, overage).
  - Legal sign-off on Marketplace terms and partner contract addendum.
  - Security review completed for tile assets (no secrets in tile metadata; icon and marketing assets scanned).
  - Partner co-sell metadata filled (MCC, partner id, named contact).
  - Support SLAs documented and playbook uploaded to listing assets.
technical_requirements: SaaS listing artifact types: For AWS — Metered SaaS + Private offers supported; ensure contract templates mapped to pricing plans.
API hooks: billing webhook endpoint must support idempotency and verify signatures from marketplace (test keys configured).
Telemetry: add metrics for trial-redemption funnel (impressions -> activate -> convert to paid) with tags: marketplace, sku, partner.
Security: no KMS keys or credentials embedded in listing assets; ensure only signed download links for logos and non-sensitive files.
Deployment options mapping: dedicated vs hosted — clearly label isolation features and any data residency constraints on tiles.
Rollout toggles: feature flag to disable trial gift for specific partners or regions.
Automated smoke tests: create nightly e2e that triggers sandbox trial redemption and verifies billing event emitted and consumed.
Compliance: ensure SOC2/ISO artifacts referenced in tile if required by partner tier.
Icon & tile specs: 1024x1024 PNG, transparent background; name files as sku-tile-<shortslug>.png.
Copy length constraints: hero = 1 line <= 120 chars; short = 80 char summary; long = 600 chars max (for AWS long description).
billing_notes: Price point guidance: provide list price + discounted partner price; Revenue Ops to confirm effective price_id for each marketplace.
Trial vouchers: voucher should be a zero-dollar invoice with a usage allowance recorded as credit line item; ensure reporting shows consumed vs remaining credit.
Metering dimensions: define primary dimension (tokens, requests, seats) and ensure we submit usage with the correct SKU identifier.
Invoice flow: test consumer invoice in sandbox, ensure invoice line-items show description friendly copy (avoid internal slugs).
copy_snippets: Hero (short): 'Enterprise LLM inference with predictable costs and fast scaling — try 14 days on us.'
Short (80 chars): 'Production-grade LLM inference — reserved or hosted, deploy in minutes.'

Long (up to 600 chars): 'Redwood Inference unifies inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so engineering teams can ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost. Start with a 14‑day trial credit to evaluate throughput and reliability under real traffic. Includes tooling for rollouts, tracing, and cost diagnostics tailored to cloud marketplaces and partner integrations.'
Tile bullets: 'Production-first runtime', 'Dedicate capacity & SLAs', 'Transparent per-token billing', 'Easy trial voucher & billing integration'
acceptance_matrix: Owner sign-offs required: Product (feature readiness), Revenue Ops (pricing), Legal (contract + tile terms), Security (asset review), SRE (smoke test pass).
Gating criteria: No open P1 bugs in listing flow, billing events passed in 3 consecutive sandbox runs, trial redemption rate instrumented, partner contact in place.
Timeline: submission -> expected marketplace review: AWS 3-7 business days, Azure 5-10 business days, build in 2 weeks buffer for legal iterations.
submission_playbook: Step 1: Finalize SKU metadata and attach all artifacts to internal PR (marketplace-assets repo).
Step 2: Run billing sandbox plan and attach screenshot logs to JIRA ticket.
Step 3: Request Legal & Security review with 'Marketplace Listing' tag and include sample contract text.
Step 4: Populate marketplace publisher portal entries (hero, short, long, screenshots, private offer config).
Step 5: Set feature flag off for promo until we confirm tile live in prod and run smoke tests.
Step 6: Post-launch: monitor trial conversion funnel daily for first 14 days, escalate any >3% drop vs baseline.
open_questions: Should trial vouchers be partner-specific or global? (Revenue Ops leaning toward partner-specific codes for attribution).
Is the reserved capacity SKU subject to minimum commitment on marketplace vs our direct billing model? Need Legal confirmation.
How will refunds from marketplace purchases be reconciled in our accounting ledger? Finance to map GCP/Azure/AWS refund flows.
next_steps: Assign GTM owner to the JIRA ticket (GT M-4321) and request Revenue Ops pricing sheet update.
Engineering: ship sandbox webhook signature support (due 2025-11-12).
Legal: confirm customer-facing terms for trial vouchers by 2025-11-14.
Partner ops: collect partner IDs for initial 3 partners and pre-provision private offers.
notes_to_self: This doc will be converted to formal checklist once the first private offer is live. Keep language vendor-agnostic where possible; include vendor-specific callouts in separate annex documents.
references: Marketplace policy: AWS SaaS Metering docs
